Senses.Explanation: Literally "go" (行) on one's "feet" (腳): "travel on foot," attested 1,333 times in 192 allowlisted texts. Chan records use it for a monk leaving one place and traveling through the various quarters, visiting monasteries and teachers. In the Ancestral Hall Collection, a monk requests permission: "I wish to travel on foot; I ask the teacher for directions" (某甲欲得行腳，乞和尚處分). Another teacher asks, "Have you come traveling on foot through the various quarters to seek the hard-to-obtain thing?" (汝諸方行腳來覓取難得底物來不). A later record explicitly says, "though traveling a thousand miles on foot, [one does so] to seek a teacher of the lineage" (千里行腳，為尋宗師). Productive forms include "person traveling on foot" (行腳人), "patch-robed monk traveling on foot" (行腳衲僧), and "leave home and travel on foot" (出家行腳).
Senses.Note: The corpus also turns the activity into a test. Asked "What is the affair of traveling on foot?" (如何是行腳事), Poshan answers, "face to face, looking at one another, the mouth is like wood" (面面相看口如木). Another instruction calls someone who has passed through a cited exchange a "true person traveling on foot" (真行腳人). No formula in the corpus makes the term a separate prescribed system.

Occurrences.Kwic: 問：「如何是行腳事？」師云：「面面相看口如木。」
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Poshan's upper-hall answer: face to face, looking at one another, the mouth is like wood.

Occurrences.Kwic: 某甲欲得行腳，乞和尚處分。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: An Ancestral Hall Collection narrative: the monk wishes to travel on foot and asks his teacher for directions.

Occurrences.Kwic: 汝諸方行腳來覓取難得底物來不？
Occurrences.AttributionNote: A teacher asks a traveler whether he came through the various quarters seeking the hard-to-obtain thing.

Occurrences.Kwic: 雖則千里行腳，為尋宗師
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Shanhui states the distance and object together: a thousand miles traveling on foot to seek a lineage teacher.

Occurrences.Kwic: 於此透過方是真行腳人
Occurrences.AttributionNote: An instruction says that passing through the preceding exchange is what makes a true person traveling on foot.
